prompt: A crate of mass 50 kg is pulled at a steady speed of 2.0 m s^-1 a distance of 10 m up a frictionless slope inclined at 30 degrees to the horizontal. The pulling force acts parallel to the slope. (Take g = 9.81 m s^-2). What is the work done on the crate by the pulling force?

answer.explanation: Because speed is constant, pulling force F balances the component of weight down the slope: F = mg sin(30 degrees) = 50 * 9.81 * 0.5 = 245.25 N. Work done W = Fs = 245.25 * 10 = 2452.5 J = 2450 J.

distractor_explanations: Correct. F = mg sin(30 degrees) = 245.25 N, W = F * s = 245.25 * 10 = 2452.5 J approx 2450 J.
Incorrect. This uses cos(30 degrees) instead of sin(30 degrees): 50 * 9.81 * cos(30 degrees) * 10 = 4248 J.
Incorrect. This forgets the slope angle and uses full weight: 50 * 9.81 * 10 = 4905 J.
Incorrect. This multiplies mass by speed and distance: 50 * 2.0 * 10 = 1000 J.
hints: The crate moves at constant speed, so resultant force along the slope is zero.
Calculate the component of weight opposing the motion along the slope.
solution: Component of weight down the incline is mg sin(30 degrees). At constant speed, pulling force F = mg sin(30 degrees) = 50 * 9.81 * 0.5 = 245.25 N. Work done W = Fs = 245.25 N * 10 m = 2452.5 J approx 2450 J (to 3 sig figs). Option A is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Show alternative approach using conservation of energy: vertical height gained h = s sin(30 degrees) = 5.0 m. W = mgh = 50 * 9.81 * 5.0 = 2452.5 J.
Reinforce why both methods yield the exact same result.
